tasks.short: Match supplier invoices to orders and receipts, resolve differences, and record the accounting entry.

steps.what: Read incoming supplier invoices and capture their details.

loop.input: Unstructured supplier invoice; structured invoices use a parser.
loop.output: Invoice fields with source locations and confidence flags.
loop.check: Validate totals, VAT arithmetic, supplier identity and duplicate keys. Matching checks follow.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per invoice; failed checks enter the exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: A parser handles structured invoices, but varied document layouts need bounded extraction.

steps.what: Find the purchase order and recorded goods or service receipt.
Compare invoice quantities, prices and totals against order and receipt records.
Resolve missing receipts, disputed prices and other invoice differences.
Approve an exception or return the invoice for correction.
Post cleared invoices with their accounting codes and supporting records.

tasks.design: Configure capture, matching tolerances and posting rules in the {ERP}, linked to orders and receipts in the {PROCUREMENT}. Use a bounded extraction loop only for unstructured invoices, and route failed checks through the {WORKFLOW} with source evidence. Matched invoices post under approved rules; disputed exceptions require the budget holder's decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Missing receipts, inconsistent invoice references and disconnected records prevented reliable matching. Existing matching functions were often only partly configured.
tasks.enabler_now: Capture and three-way matching already exist. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building adapters, validation checks and exception views.
tasks.still_hard: Service receipts, partial deliveries, disputed charges and unreliable supplier records still need people. Extraction cannot establish that a service was delivered.
tasks.human_edge: Establish what was actually received and negotiate a fair resolution when the records disagree.

ambition.what: Daily decision on which missing receipts threaten the next payment run.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time resolving blocked purchases and less time copying invoice fields. They can prioritise exceptions within policy; spending and payment authority do not expand automatically.

reach.task: Review supplier accruals at period end.
reach.learn: Cut-off rules, receipt evidence and the difference between an invoice delay and an unrecorded liability.

evidence.claim: Invoice capture can identify suppliers using registration, VAT and bank details.
Line-level matching of invoices, orders and receipts is an existing capability.
A vendor case reports automatic processing rising from 40% to 65% nine months after implementation.
Manual and email invoice approval remain common in the cited survey; its sample is not a European prevalence estimate.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: The baseline is an order-backed invoice process; non-order invoices need a separate coding and approval path.
Exception steps are weighted across the invoice workload, rather than occurring on every invoice.
The model covers checking time in the matching step rather than treating all verification as document handling.
Posting under approved matching rules is permitted; posting does not release payment.
Build ranges assume existing capture and matching functions. Missing interfaces increase integration effort.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; national rules determine any employee consultation needed for changed work practices.
unknowns: Which matching, capture and interface functions are licensed and enabled?
How often are receipts missing, and who can confirm service delivery?
Which tolerances, accounting codes and posting permissions are approved?
What document-processing access, retention rules and national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: How well does the available extraction capability perform on the relevant invoice layouts and languages?
new_work: Review failed extraction checks and unresolved matches.
Maintain supplier identifiers, tolerances and accounting mappings.
Monitor duplicate prevention, posting failures and interface changes.
Sample automatic postings and investigate recurring receipt gaps.

tasks.short: Collect approved payroll changes, process the pay run, resolve warnings and prepare payroll outputs.

steps.what: Collect approved employee, contract and absence changes for the payroll period.
Consolidate approved hours, overtime and variable pay from departmental returns.
Enter or import changes and check that all expected records arrived.
Calculate draft pay and generate validation and period comparison reports.
Investigate warnings, confirm entitlements and correct approved payroll inputs.
Approve the checked payroll and lock the run.
Release payslips to employees through the employee portal.
Transfer the payroll journal and prepare payment instructions.

tasks.design: Connect approved changes from the {HCM} to the {PAYROLL}, with a validated {WORKFLOW} for variable pay. Configure calculations, comparison checks and journal transfers to the {ERP}; people resolve entitlement questions, approve the run and release payslips. Send the payroll payment batch into the separately authorised payment process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Late departmental inputs, inconsistent pay codes and unclear approvals made imports unreliable. Payroll calculation itself was already supported by specialist software.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing payroll checks and interfaces cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding makes validated input forms and adapters cheaper to build; no model is needed for wage arithmetic.
tasks.still_hard: Entitlements, retroactive changes, collective agreements and national rules need maintained payroll expertise. A technically valid calculation can still use the wrong approved input.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a pay result is unfair or legally wrong, establish the employee's entitlement and handle sensitive corrections.

ambition.what: Weekly payroll readiness decision before the period closes.

tasks.altitude: The clerk can investigate missing approvals throughout the month instead of concentrating data entry near payday. They can assess readiness and recommend corrections; payroll approval and payment release remain designated decisions.

reach.task: Reconcile payroll liabilities to ledger balances.
reach.learn: Payroll control accounts, accruals, clearing items and journal reconciliation.
Separate headcount, pay-rate, overtime and timing effects without exposing individual pay unnecessarily.

evidence.claim: Existing payroll software provides run checks covering salary changes.
Existing payroll software compares outputs across three periods per employee.
Dutch works-council consent rules cover specified employee-data and monitoring arrangements; national rules elsewhere differ.
The digest provides payroll capabilities but no documented payroll implementation outcome.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: The clerk supports an established payroll function rather than replacing payroll expertise.
Departmental variable-pay returns still require consolidation; core employee records are already structured.
Approved changes are distinguishable from requests awaiting approval.
Bank payment release and statutory filing are separate downstream tasks.
Testing includes representative historical periods and a parallel run before release.
GDPR applies to employee data. The EU AI Act applies where relevant; this design does not score or monitor employees with a model.
The access range includes consultation work where national rules require it; formal consultation can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which national rules, agreements and payroll calendars apply?
Which variable-pay inputs already arrive through approved structured records?
Who can approve payroll changes, lock runs and release payslips?
Which interfaces, test environments and historical payroll records are accessible?
Does the proposed change require employee or works-council consultation?
research_questions: Which supported interfaces preserve effective dates, corrections and payroll audit history?
new_work: Resolve rejected imports and missing departmental approvals.
Maintain pay-code mappings and validation rules.
Check rule updates with the payroll specialist.
Monitor journal reconciliation and access logs.
Review readiness exceptions before the payroll deadline.

tasks.short: Balance cashier receipts, prepare physical deposits and reconcile the bank credit.

steps.what: Produce cashier closing summaries from the point-of-sale system.
Receive sealed takings, count cash and record custody.
Balance counted takings against cashier summaries and separate non-cash receipts.
Investigate discrepancies with the cashier and record the agreed explanation.
Prepare the deposit slip and custody paperwork.
Approve and hand the sealed deposit to the authorised collection service.
Match the bank credit to the deposit and update cash clearing.

tasks.design: Import point-of-sale closing records from the {OTHER} into a deposit register in the {WORKFLOW}. Deterministic checks balance recorded counts, generate deposit paperwork and match bank credits from the {BANK} to clearing entries in the {ERP}. People count physical cash, resolve discrepancies and approve its handover.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical custody cannot be replaced by software. Disconnected closing reports, paper custody records and bank references also created avoidable clerical work.
tasks.enabler_now: Standard exports and bank feeds can connect the records. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building a small deposit register and document generator.
tasks.still_hard: Cash must still be counted, secured and transported. A balanced digital record cannot prove the contents of a sealed bag.
tasks.human_edge: Maintain custody, notice physical irregularities and investigate differences fairly without assuming misconduct.

ambition.what: Daily escalation decision for deposits that have not received the expected bank credit.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time balancing reports and preparing slips, while physical cash work remains. They can prioritise delayed-credit investigations; deposit limits and write-off authority need explicit delegation.

reach.task: Monitor cash in transit and expected available funds.
reach.learn: Settlement timing, bank cut-offs, custody exposure and cash-clearing reconciliation.

evidence.claim: Bank matching on references and other identifiers is an existing capability, with unmatched items sent to people.
Deposit balancing and paperwork can use deterministic rules; physical cash custody remains human work.
The digest provides no documented case for automating this physical deposit workflow.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies to a business with physical takings; many mid-size companies have no such workflow.
Electronic card receipts settle separately and are excluded from the physical deposit.
Cheques are included only where local banking practice and the receiving bank support them.
Physical counting and custody take more time than the supplied means prior suggests.
A standard closing report is available from the point-of-sale system, represented by {OTHER}.
GDPR applies to named cashier records. National rules determine consultation requirements if the change alters employee monitoring.
Discrepancy records support reconciliation, not automated employee scoring.
unknowns: What volumes and forms of physical takings exist?
What counting equipment, custody controls and collection arrangements are already used?
Can closing records and bank credits share a stable deposit reference?
Who approves shortages, adjustments and deposit handovers?
Would named cashier reporting change existing monitoring arrangements?
research_questions: Which receiving-bank references and collection-service records support reliable deposit matching?
new_work: Investigate unmatched or short bank credits.
Maintain closing-record mappings and deposit reference rules.
Check duplicate imports and missing custody records.
Maintain templates when bank deposit requirements change.

tasks.short: Calculate amounts due, prepare payment batches and obtain authorised release.

steps.what: Select approved invoices and other liabilities approaching their due dates.
Calculate tax and recurring payment amounts from approved schedules and assessments.
Prepare the payment proposal with due dates, discounts, holds and available funds.
Verify changed beneficiary details through an independently sourced contact.
Create and upload the payment batch for bank authorisation.
Review the payment batch and authorise bank release.
Record settled payments and investigate rejected or unmatched transactions.

tasks.design: Configure the {ERP} to select approved liabilities, apply payment rules and stage batches in the {BANK}. A deterministic generator calculates amounts from approved tax and recurring-payment schedules, while the {WORKFLOW} records exceptions and beneficiary verification. An authorised signatory releases funds, and bank statements reconcile settled payments back to the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Payment rules and approvals were split between records, workbooks and bank screens. Concerns about releasing money often prevented automation of preparation as well.
tasks.enabler_now: Payment proposals, bank batch formats and statement matching are established capabilities. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting approved schedules and producing control reports.
tasks.still_hard: Tax interpretation, disputed liabilities, cash shortages and beneficiary fraud need accountable decisions. Bank access and signatory arrangements can dominate implementation time.
tasks.human_edge: Decide which obligations need attention when cash is constrained, verify unusual requests and accept responsibility for releasing money.

ambition.what: Daily recommendation on payment timing when available cash is constrained.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time calculating and uploading batches and more time explaining holds, deadlines and cash constraints. They can recommend payment timing; bank release rights remain with authorised signatories.

reach.learn: Value dates, settlement cut-offs, committed outflows and liquidity buffers.

reach.task: Reconcile tax payments to approved returns and assessments.
reach.learn: Payment references, tax periods and the boundary between calculation and tax interpretation.

evidence.claim: Automatic bank matching using references and identifiers is an existing capability.
Payment calculations and batch preparation can use deterministic rules while bank release remains human.
Electronic payment batches are a more suitable baseline than routine cheque preparation for this European company profile.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: Electronic transfers replace the cheque wording in the source task; physical cheques are an exception.
Tax specialists approve tax treatment and schedules before payment calculations use them.
Beneficiary changes follow a separate controlled master-data approval process before batch creation.
Staging a batch cannot release funds, and approval binds to the exact batch version and control totals.
Standing instructions are already authorised and are not re-created as new ad hoc payments.
The final reconciliation step reviews unmatched cases; exact settlements can post automatically.
GDPR applies to personal bank details. National rules determine any consultation required for changed employee-data handling.
unknowns: Which banks, payment formats and staging interfaces are available?
What signatory limits, dual approvals and payment cut-offs apply?
Who approves tax schedules and beneficiary master-data changes?
How often do cash constraints require payment prioritisation?
Are physical cheques still required for any payment category?
What access and employee consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Does the bank interface preserve approval controls and expose reliable batch and settlement identifiers?
new_work: Maintain payment calendars, calculation rules and bank mappings.
Review calculation exceptions and rejected payments.
Verify beneficiary changes and maintain the evidence trail.
Monitor duplicate-payment controls and batch integrity.
Reconcile payment failures and unexpected settlement dates.

role.altitude: The role shifts from copying and calculating toward maintaining reliable transaction flows and resolving exceptions. Clerks gain better grounds to recommend priorities and corrections; spending, payroll approval, cash custody and payment release retain explicit authority limits.
reach: Accountant: reconcile payroll liabilities, supplier accruals and clearing accounts.
Treasurer: explain cash in transit, settlement delays and upcoming outflows.
Budget analyst: explain personnel-cost changes using approved, appropriately aggregated records.
Tax preparer: reconcile payments to approved tax schedules and assessments.
skills_to_grow: Control totals, reconciliations and accounting cut-off.
Exception investigation and clear evidence gathering.
Import validation, reference mapping and duplicate prevention.
Payroll entitlement boundaries and sensitive employee communication.
Cash timing, beneficiary verification and approval controls.
GDPR, relevant EU AI Act duties and applicable national consultation rules.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a daily finance readiness service covering blocked invoices, payroll inputs, cash in transit and payments due. Give each exception an accountable owner, supporting evidence and a recommended next action within the clerk's authority.
